div.span: my commit history tells the real story
it compiles. mostly.
i write firmware. also the backend. also the frontend.
i have a bambu lab x1c and a problem with starting new projects
full-stack, bottom to top
yes those OBS scenes have custom animated backgrounds. i made them.
yes, i control my 3d printer through a custom AI assistant
my dad wanted to control the hot tub on his phone. so i built it.
it began with how hard could it be
i like projects with sharp edges
i think about edge cases in the shower
happiest when there's solder in the air
i once debugged a wake stub at 2am. would do it again.
firmware engineer who forgot to stop at the backend
if it's broken, i'm already fixing it
my commit times say a lot about my sleep schedule
building an open-source robot arm. currently in pieces.
i care a lot about the things i make
always building something
sometimes i read the datasheet twice
i just wanted to check the bus times
i added OTA updates. then a web portal. then...
git blame says i did that. git blame is correct.
built a full streaming setup. purely for vibes.
that feeling when the e-ink refreshes exactly right
i told myself i'd keep it simple this time
i spent hours on OBS overlays i never go live with
i speak microcontroller and server fluently
every project starts with a folder and a dream
the boring parts of a project are still my problem
i have custom OBS overlays for coding, electronics, and gaming
added one more feature. and then one more. and then one more.
my OBS setup is production-ready. i don't stream.
i volunteer at things and accidentally ship software
still learning. always building.
